Read-only terminal audit pass 1 rerun for Bundjil. Worktree: /Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil. Use gpt-5.6-sol high. Do not edit files, commit, run provider calls, or mutate anything.

Review the complete current working-tree candidate relative to origin/main, with emphasis on the corrections for ENP-AUDIT-001..004 and all affected call paths. This is ordered pass 1 only: Effect contracts, Schemas, branded ingress/egress, typed errors, Config, Layers, provider adapters, secret-negative telemetry, raw transport exposure, and direct-proof semantics.

Mandatory:
- Read AGENTS.md, docs/README.md, the active Effect SPEC/task ledger/plan, strict-effect-ts and effect-client-wrapper skills.
- Use installed effect@4.0.0-beta.101 as authority and inspect the local Effect v4 clone at revision 1caab3cc30f626efbf15e59d74f539a487e5c85c where needed. Never use Effect v3 guidance.
- Trace callers/consumers, package exports, live/local/testing Layers, and tests.
- Verify the Photon structured diagnostic cannot retain provider-controlled strings.
- Verify Codex tool parameters are object-root recursive JSON on both input/provider sides.
- Verify raw Codex HTTP/SSE services and byte streams do not escape supported public exports, while production and tests compose correctly.
- Verify direct proof rejects non-SSE/malformed/incomplete success and requires decoded response.completed.
- Look for additional pass-1 defects across the touched candidate, not merely those four.
- Report findings first, ordered by severity, with exact file:line references and consequence. If no findings, say so explicitly and list the exact invariants inspected and residual proof limits.
- Do not treat local checks as provider/Production proof.

I’ll audit the specified worktree without mutations, establish the exact diff against `origin/main`, then trace the affected contracts through exports, Layers, adapters, consumers, and tests. I’ll keep repository proof separate from any provider or production claim.

The candidate is a large branch plus an additional uncommitted correction set; `origin/main` is the merge base, so both committed and working-tree changes are in scope. The prior audit history identifies raw Codex transport and buffered SSE concerns, but I’m treating that only as orientation and checking the current candidate directly.

The active ledger defines the four correction contracts precisely: closed Photon telemetry; recursive JSON object tool parameters on both sides; no supported raw Codex transport export; and proof success only after decoding `response.completed`. I’m now checking implementation and consumer topology against those semantics, including whether the tests prove the real public paths rather than internal seams.

The object-root recursive JSON contract is present on both the OpenAI-compatible ingress and Codex provider request, and the live HTTP adapter re-encodes the owned request Schema before egress. Two boundary details need closer scrutiny: Layer composition uses `provideMerge`, which can retain private services in exported Layers, and the proof’s MIME check is currently substring-based.

A controlled hostile-rejection probe exposed an additional Photon defect: the diagnostic fields are closed, but `Reflect.get` can execute a provider-controlled getter inside the `tryPromise` catch mapper. That turns the expected failure into an Effect defect carrying the provider’s thrown message, bypassing both the tagged error and the secret-negative logger contract.

The direct proof also accepts an unterminated SSE data line as a completed event, even though no SSE event boundary was observed, and accepts a non-SSE media type when `text/event-stream` appears only in a parameter. Both controlled cases returned `Success`, so ENP-AUDIT-004 is not closed.

I’ve separated the direct-proof defect from the live streaming path: the former can falsely certify a response, while the latter appears able to synthesize a clean OpenAI completion when upstream ends without `response.completed`. I’m validating that second path in memory, then I’ll finish the public-Layer and Vercel adapter call-graph review.
Please conclude this pass now with findings or explicit no-findings and residual limits. Do not continue broad exploration.

**Findings**

1. **[P1] Live streaming fabricates successful completion after an incomplete upstream response.**  
   [stream-mapper.ts:315](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/codex/src/provider/stream-mapper.ts:315) accepts an unterminated final SSE line, while [stream-mapper.ts:326](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/codex/src/provider/stream-mapper.ts:326) unconditionally appends a `stop`/`tool_calls` chunk and `[DONE]`. It never requires a decoded `response.completed`. An in-memory probe with only an unterminated text delta produced the delta, `finish_reason: "stop"`, and `[DONE]`. Consequently, the production proxy can present truncated provider output as a clean completion.

2. **[P1] Direct proof still accepts non-SSE and incomplete SSE success.**  
   [http-client.ts:105](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/codex/src/provider/http-client.ts:105) uses substring matching for the media type, so `application/json; note=text/event-stream` passes. [http-client.ts:114](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/codex/src/provider/http-client.ts:114) processes individual lines instead of dispatched SSE events, so an unterminated `data: {"type":"response.completed"}` line also passes the final check at [http-client.ts:140](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/codex/src/provider/http-client.ts:140). Both cases returned success in controlled probes. ENP-AUDIT-004 is therefore not closed.

3. **[P1] Photon provider accessors can bypass the typed, secret-negative error boundary.**  
   [client.ts:67](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/photon/src/client.ts:67) uses unguarded `Reflect.get` while deriving the closed diagnostic at [client.ts:75](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/photon/src/client.ts:75). A provider-controlled `cause` getter that throws escaped as the raw `Error("provider-getter-secret")`, bypassing both the tagged failure and diagnostic sanitisation at [client.ts:95](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/photon/src/client.ts:95). The diagnostic schema itself contains no provider strings, but its producer does not safely inspect hostile values. ENP-AUDIT-001 remains open.

4. **[P2] Exported Codex Layers retain private transport services.**  
   `CodexResponsesProofLive` and the direct-provider Layers use `Layer.provideMerge` at [runtime.ts:351](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/codex/src/runtime.ts:351), [runtime.ts:376](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/codex/src/runtime.ts:376), and [runtime.ts:393](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/codex/src/runtime.ts:393). Effect v4 defines this operation as retaining provided services. Runtime inspection confirmed the resulting context includes `CodexHttpClient`, `CodexRequestMapper`, and `CodexStreamMapper`. The testing Layers repeat this at [testing/index.ts:95](/Users/cooper/.codex/worktrees/d4b4e069-1303-427d-957e-756d18e049a9/bundjil/packages/codex/src/testing/index.ts:95). Root export-name tests do not inspect Layer outputs, so ENP-AUDIT-003 is not closed.

**Inspected Invariants**

- Codex tool parameters use recursive `Schema.Json` values beneath an object root on both OpenAI ingress and provider egress. Nested objects work; array/null roots and non-JSON values are rejected. No defect found for ENP-AUDIT-002.
- Photon’s encoded structured diagnostic has only closed operation/phase values, bounded integers, booleans, and `unknown` sentinels.
- Installed `effect@4.0.0-beta.101` and the clean local Effect clone at revision `1caab3cc30f626efbf15e59d74f539a487e5c85c` were used as authority.
- Package exports, production/testing Layer composition, direct-provider consumers, and focused correction tests were traced.

No files were edited and no provider calls were made. These are repository and in-memory local proofs only. I did not run full verification because this was a strict read-only pass, and I stopped further broad exploration when requested; none of this establishes provider or Production behaviour.
